docs.title: Level-aware deep recursive ensemble learning
docs.text:
RocketStack turns flat model stacking into a vertically recursive learning architecture for binary and multiclass classification. The published Python package brings the research implementation into a clean, reusable API.

Try the simple example View on PyPI Source on GitHub

Install the official release

pip install rocketstack_ensemble_ai

docs.title: Why RocketStack?
docs.text:
Traditional stacking combines predictions in a single meta-learning stage. RocketStack instead builds successive levels: out-of-fold probability features are propagated into deeper representations, feature growth is controlled, and the active learner pool is refined between levels.

  • Recursive stacking: probability features move through successive meta-learning levels.
  • Level-aware pruning: the blurrization heuristic introduces controlled score perturbation and removes weaker learners between levels.
  • Intermediate feature processing: stochastic feature elimination, autoencoder reduction, and attention-based selection are supported.
  • Diverse learner pool: scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost models participate in the ensemble.
  • Reusable models: the public API provides familiar fit, predict, predict_proba, and score workflows.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: RocketStack supports Python 3.10–3.13.

docs.title: Install from PyPI
docs.text:
The official release is available from the Python Package Index:

pip install rocketstack_ensemble_ai

View RocketStack on PyPI

The complete model pool uses NumPy, scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Optuna, and TensorFlow. These dependencies are installed automatically, so the first installation can take a few minutes.

docs.title: Verify the installation
docs.text:
python -c "import rocketstack_ensemble_ai; print(rocketstack_ensemble_ai.__version__)"

For the current release, this prints:

0.1.0

docs.title: Install the latest GitHub source
docs.text:
Use this only when you specifically want the newest repository version rather than the published PyPI release:

pip install "git+https://github.com/caghangir-1/RocketStack-Ensemble-Architecture-ai.git"

docs.title: Simple example
docs.text:
This example assumes that your data is already divided into training and test sets:

  • X_train and X_test contain the predictor variables.
  • y_train and y_test contain the corresponding target labels.

No demonstration or mock dataset is created here—the same pattern can be applied directly to your own prepared data.

docs.title: 1. Install RocketStack
docs.text: pip install rocketstack_ensemble_ai

docs.title: 2. Binary classification
docs.text:
Import the branded binary model factory and choose the desired recursion level:

from rocketstack_ensemble_ai import ascentTheRocket_binary_model

model = ascentTheRocket_binary_model(
    level=3,
    return_model="best",
    iffeatselection=False,
    blur_strength="light",
    n_jobs=-1,
)

Fit the model with the training split, then generate predictions and class probabilities for the test split:

model.fit(X_train, y_train)

y_pred = model.predict(X_test)
y_prob = model.predict_proba(X_test)
test_score = model.score(X_test, y_test)

print(f"Test accuracy: {test_score:.3f}")

y_pred contains the predicted class for every row in X_test. y_prob contains the corresponding class probabilities.

docs.title: 3. Multiclass classification
docs.text:
For targets containing more than two classes, use the multiclass factory:

from rocketstack_ensemble_ai import ascentTheRocket_multiclass_model

model = ascentTheRocket_multiclass_model(
    level=3,
    return_model="best",
    iffeatselection_or_not=False,
    n_jobs=-1,
)

model.fit(X_train, y_train)
y_pred = model.predict(X_test)
y_prob = model.predict_proba(X_test)
test_score = model.score(X_test, y_test)

docs.title: Class-based alternative
docs.text:
The same branded model factories are available through the RocketStack class:

from rocketstack_ensemble_ai import RocketStack

rocket = RocketStack()
model = rocket.ascentTheRocket_binary_model(
    level=3,
    return_model="best",
)

model.fit(X_train, y_train)
y_pred = model.predict(X_test)

Keep the test set separate

Fit RocketStack only with X_train and y_train. Use X_test and y_test after training for an unbiased evaluation of the fitted model.
